examples.en: If smoke is detected, an alarm goes off.
A small earthquake was detected last night.

examples.ko: 센서에 사람의 움직임이 감지돼서 불이 켜졌어요.
examples.en: The sensor detected a person's movement, so the light turned on.

examples.ko: 이상한 소리가 감지되는 순간 기계가 멈췄어요.
examples.en: The moment a strange sound was detected, the machine stopped.
We are analyzing the signal that was detected.

examples.ko: 병원 검사에서 아무 문제도 감지되지 않았어요.
examples.en: No problems were detected in the hospital test.

explain: 기계, 센서, 검사가 눈에 안 띄는 신호나 변화를 알아챘다는 뜻이에요. 사람이 느끼는 건 '느끼다', 기계가 알아채는 건 '감지되다'를 써요. 뉴스에서는 지진, 연기, 소음, 이상 징후 이야기에 자주 나와요.
explain_en: A machine, sensor or test picks up a signal or change that isn't obvious. When a person feels it, use 느끼다, and when equipment catches it, use 감지되다. In news it often appears with earthquakes, smoke, noise and warning signs.

examples.ko: 어릴 때 생긴 버릇이 어른이 되면 고착돼요.
examples.en: A habit formed in childhood becomes fixed once you are an adult.

examples.ko: 잘못된 자세가 고착되기 전에 고쳐야 해요.
examples.en: You should fix a bad posture before it becomes set.
In that region, poverty has become entrenched.
Once an image becomes fixed, it is hard to change.

examples.ko: 성별에 대한 편견이 고착되어 있다는 지적이 나왔어요.
examples.en: People pointed out that prejudice about gender has become entrenched.

examples.ko: 시험 방식 때문에 암기식 공부가 고착됐어요.
examples.en: Because of the exam format, studying by memorization has become the norm.

explain: '굳어지다'와 비슷하지만 더 딱딱한 말이고, 나쁜 습관이나 편견처럼 바뀌기 어려운 상태가 될 때 많이 써요. '고착화되다'라고도 해요.
explain_en: It is similar to '굳어지다' but more formal, and it is often used when something like a bad habit or prejudice settles into a state that is hard to change. You can also say '고착화되다'.

dis.h: becomes stuck or entrenched, hard to change

p.n: 고정되다 means set in place; it does not carry the sense of a habit becoming entrenched.

en: be realized; be implemented; be embodied

examples.en: The new feature will be implemented next week.
The designer's idea was realized just as it was.

examples.ko: 꿈이 현실로 구현되는 날이 올 거예요.
examples.en: The day will come when the dream becomes reality.
This feature hasn't been implemented yet.
The world in the game was recreated as if it were real.
Please wait until the plan is carried out.

explain: '만들어지다'보다 딱딱하고, 계획이나 아이디어, 기능이 실제로 나타난다는 말이에요. 컴퓨터, 디자인, 정책 이야기에 자주 나와요. 만드는 쪽은 '구현하다'예요.
explain_en: Stiffer than '만들어지다'; it says a plan, idea or feature has actually appeared. Common in talk about computing, design and policy. The maker's side is '구현하다'.

examples.en: The whole world watched the spacecraft return.
The airport was crowded at the news of the team's return.
I'm worried because the return date hasn't been set.

examples.ko: 오랜 여행 끝에 마침내 귀환이 이루어졌어요.
examples.en: After a long journey, the return finally happened.
I watched a movie called The Hero's Return.
Everyone prayed for the probe's safe return.

explain: 멀리 갔던 사람이나 우주선, 군대가 원래 있던 곳으로 돌아오는 일에 격식 있게 써요. 일상에서 집에 돌아올 때는 '귀가'나 '돌아오다'를 써요. '무사 귀환'이라는 말을 자주 들어요.
explain_en: A formal word for a person, spacecraft, or army coming back to where it started after going far away. For coming home in daily life use '귀가' or '돌아오다'. You often hear the phrase '무사 귀환' (safe return).

examples.ko: 까딱하면 지각할 것 같아서 택시를 탔어요.
examples.en: I might easily be late, so I took a taxi.

examples.ko: 길이 얼어서 까딱하면 넘어질 수 있어요.
examples.en: The road is icy, so you could easily fall with one wrong step.

examples.ko: 이 일은 까딱하면 큰 사고로 이어져요.
examples.en: One slip in this job can lead to a big accident.
With just a little carelessness, I almost lost the important documents.

examples.ko: 요즘 같은 날씨에는 까딱하면 감기에 걸려요.
examples.en: In weather like this, you catch a cold if you're the slightest bit careless.

examples.ko: 까딱하면 약속을 잊을 것 같아서 메모해 놨어요.
examples.en: I might easily forget the appointment, so I made a note of it.

explain: 조금만 잘못하면 나쁜 결과가 생길 수 있을 때 써요. 보통 뒤에 '-ㄹ 뻔했다', '-ㄹ 수 있다', '-ㄹ 것 같다'가 와요. 좋은 결과를 말할 때는 쓰지 않아요.
explain_en: Use it when a small mistake could lead to a bad result. It is usually followed by '-ㄹ 뻔했다', '-ㄹ 수 있다' or '-ㄹ 것 같다'. It is not used for good outcomes.

examples.en: The speed of the fall gets faster and faster.
We confirmed the falling of objects through an experiment.
The parachute drop training has started.
I filmed the ball dropping.
They hit the landing point exactly.
They put up a safety net to prevent falling accidents.

explain: 위에서 아래로 떨어지는 것을 과학이나 훈련 이야기에서 말해요. 일상에서는 '떨어지다'를 쓰고, '낙하'는 '낙하산', '자유 낙하', '낙하 사고'처럼 굳은 말에서 자주 나와요.
explain_en: It is the dropping of something from above, used in science and training contexts. In daily speech people say 떨어지다; 낙하 appears in set terms such as 낙하산 (parachute), 자유 낙하, and 낙하 사고.

examples.ko: 관중이 경기장에 난입해서 경기가 잠시 멈췄어요.
examples.en: A spectator burst onto the field, so the game stopped for a moment.
A stranger suddenly barged into the meeting room.

examples.ko: 고양이가 무대에 난입하는 바람에 모두 웃었어요.
examples.en: A cat wandered onto the stage and everyone laughed.
Fans tried to storm the venue but were stopped by security guards.

examples.ko: 방송 중에 아이가 스튜디오에 난입한 영상이 화제예요.
examples.en: A video of a child bursting into the studio during a broadcast is a hot topic.
I locked the door so people couldn't barge in.

explain: 허락 없이 갑자기, 막무가내로 들어올 때 써요. 그냥 '들어오다'와 달리 소란스럽고 예의 없는 느낌이 있어서 뉴스에서 '경기장에 난입하다'처럼 많이 보여요. 비슷한 말로 '쳐들어오다'가 있어요.
explain_en: It is used when someone comes in suddenly and unceremoniously without permission. Unlike plain '들어오다', it feels noisy and rude, and appears in news as in '경기장에 난입하다'. A similar word is '쳐들어오다'.

en: be found out; be revealed; come to light (something hidden)

examples.en: What I did in secret was found out in the end.
The thief in hiding gets discovered by the police.
If cheating on an exam is discovered, you are in big trouble.
I was worried the secret would come to light.
Only after being found out did he tell the truth.
I tried not to get caught, but it ended up being discovered.

explain: '들키다'는 일상에서 누구에게나 쓰고, '발각되다'는 나쁜 일이나 비밀이 드러났을 때 뉴스나 글에서 더 많이 써요. 친구나 가족에게 걸렸을 때는 '들켰어요'가 자연스러워요.
explain_en: '들키다' is the everyday word for getting caught, while '발각되다' is used more in news and writing when something bad or secret comes out. When your friend or family catches you, '들켰어요' sounds more natural.

en: be emitted; be discharged; (a player) be released from a team

examples.en: Harmful gas is released from the factory.
Heat in the body is released through sweat.
A large amount of energy was released all at once.

examples.ko: 방출된 물질은 바람을 타고 멀리 퍼졌어요.
examples.en: The released substance spread far on the wind.

examples.ko: 구단에서 방출되면 새 팀을 찾아야 해요.
examples.en: If you are let go by the club, you have to find a new team.
I attached a filter so smoke does not escape.

explain: 방출되다는 열·가스·에너지가 밖으로 나오는 결과를 말할 때 써요. 같은 뜻으로 '나오다', '빠져나가다'가 쉬운 말이에요. 선수가 팀에서 나가게 될 때도 '방출되다'라고 해요.
explain_en: 방출되다 describes heat, gas or energy ending up released outward; the easier everyday words are '나오다' and '빠져나가다'. A player let go by a team is also '방출되다'.

examples.ko: 집에 무슨 변고가 생긴 것 같아요.
examples.en: It seems something terrible has happened at home.
I arrived safely without any trouble.

examples.ko: 갑자기 연락이 끊겨서 변고가 있는지 걱정돼요.
examples.en: Contact suddenly stopped, so I'm worried something has happened.

examples.ko: 이 마을에 큰 변고가 일어난 적이 있어요.
examples.en: A major disaster once happened in this village.

examples.ko: 변고를 알리는 전화를 받고 급히 달려갔어요.
examples.en: I got a call about the bad news and rushed over.
The day passed without anything unusual happening.

explain: 갑자기 생긴 나쁜 일을 말하고, '변고 없이'처럼 아무 일 없다는 말로 자주 써요. '사고'보다 무슨 일인지 막연한 느낌이에요. 놀랄 때 '이게 무슨 변고야?'라고도 해요.
explain_en: It refers to a sudden bad event and is often used in the negative sense of '변고 없이' (without incident). Compared with '사고' (accident), it feels vaguer about what exactly happened. People also exclaim '이게 무슨 변고야?' when shocked.

examples.en: If you spend money carelessly, it's gone quickly.
I'm sorry for losing my temper without thinking.
You shouldn't believe rumors without discernment.
He recklessly talked about other people's secrets.
The kids are running around recklessly, which is dangerous.
Don't make promises without thinking.

explain: 앞뒤를 따져 보지 않고 행동한다는 느낌이에요. '함부로'와 비슷한데, '함부로'가 더 일상적이고 '분별없이'는 조금 딱딱해요. '쓰다, 믿다, 말하다, 행동하다' 같은 동사와 자주 어울려요.
explain_en: It gives the feeling of acting without weighing things up. It is similar to '함부로', but '함부로' is more everyday and '분별없이' is a bit stiffer. It pairs often with verbs like '쓰다', '믿다', '말하다' and '행동하다'.

examples.en: This year's budget has all been used up.

examples.ko: 하루 일을 마치니 체력이 다 소진됐어요.
examples.en: After finishing the day's work, my energy was completely drained.

examples.ko: 인기 상품은 며칠 만에 소진될 거예요.
examples.en: Popular items will run out within a few days.
The coupons ran out quickly, so I couldn't get one.
Charge it before the battery runs out.
I rested for a week to recover my depleted energy.

explain: 소진되다는 힘, 예산, 재고처럼 쓰는 것이 자연스럽게 모두 줄어서 없어질 때 써요. 내가 일부러 다 쓴 게 아니라 '그렇게 되었다'는 느낌이에요. 일상 대화에서는 '다 떨어졌어요'가 더 흔하고, 공지나 뉴스에서 소진되다를 자주 봐요.
explain_en: Sojindoeda is used when energy, budget, or stock gradually gets fully used up, as a state that came about rather than something you did on purpose. In daily talk 다 떨어졌어요 is more common, while notices and news often use 소진되다.

examples.en: The computer broke down, and the data was lost.
Some of the crops are lost because of the rain.

examples.ko: 손실된 금액은 보험으로 보상받을 수 있어요.
examples.en: You can be compensated by insurance for the lost amount.
Many cultural properties are lost to fires.

examples.ko: 열이 새 나가면 에너지가 손실될 거예요.
examples.en: If heat escapes, energy will be lost.

examples.ko: 파일이 손실되면 처음부터 다시 만들어야 해요.
examples.en: If the file is lost, you have to remake it from the start.

explain: 돈, 데이터, 에너지, 재산 같은 것이 줄어들거나 없어질 때 써요. '잃어버리다'는 내가 물건을 놓친 느낌이고 '손실되다'는 손해를 보는 객관적인 말이에요. 회사 보고서나 뉴스에서 자주 봐요.
explain_en: Used when something like money, data, energy or property decreases or disappears. 잃어버리다 feels like you personally lost an item, while 손실되다 is a more objective word for taking a loss. It is common in company reports and news.

en: lose one's footing; miss one's step; slip down

examples.en: I lost my footing on the trail while hiking and hurt my leg.

examples.ko: 비 오는 날에는 계단에서 실족하기 쉬워요.
examples.en: It is easy to slip on stairs on rainy days.

examples.ko: 그는 바위에서 실족했지만 다행히 크게 다치지 않았어요.
examples.en: He lost his footing on a rock, but fortunately he was not badly hurt.
I almost lost my footing on the snowy road yesterday.
If you slip and fall in the mountains, call 119 right away.

examples.ko: 어두운 길에서 실족하지 않게 손전등을 챙겼어요.
examples.en: I brought a flashlight so I would not slip on the dark path.

explain: 산길, 계단, 물가처럼 위험한 곳에서 발을 잘못 디뎌 넘어지거나 떨어질 때 써요. 일상 대화에서는 '발을 헛디디다'라고 더 자주 말하고, '실족하다'는 뉴스나 안전 안내문에서 많이 보여요.
explain_en: It is used when you misstep and fall at dangerous places such as mountain trails, stairs or waterfronts. In daily conversation people more often say '발을 헛디디다', while '실족하다' appears a lot in the news and safety notices.

examples.ko: 약물 오용은 건강에 큰 문제가 돼요.
examples.en: Drug misuse is a serious problem for your health.

examples.ko: 단어 오용 때문에 뜻이 이상하게 전달됐어요.
examples.en: The meaning came across strangely because of the misuse of a word.

examples.ko: 권한 오용으로 그 공무원은 조사를 받았어요.
examples.en: That official was investigated for misuse of authority.

examples.ko: 항생제 오용을 막기 위해 의사의 처방이 필요해요.
examples.en: A doctor's prescription is needed to prevent the misuse of antibiotics.

examples.ko: 맞춤법에서 자주 보이는 오용 사례를 정리했어요.
examples.en: I put together common examples of misuse in spelling.

examples.ko: 장비 오용으로 사고가 난 적이 있어요.
examples.en: There was once an accident caused by the misuse of equipment.

explain: 약, 권한, 말처럼 쓰는 방법이 정해진 것을 틀리게 쓸 때 써요. '남용'은 지나치게 많이 쓴다는 쪽이라서 '오용'과 달라요.
explain_en: It is used when something with a proper way of use, like medicine, authority or words, is used wrongly. '남용' (overuse) is about using too much, so it differs from '오용'.

en: leave; deviate from; break away from

examples.en: The train went off the track.

examples.ko: 선수 한 명이 대열에서 이탈한 걸 아무도 몰랐어요.
examples.en: Nobody noticed that one player had dropped out of the line.
Leaving the path is dangerous, so follow the signs.

examples.ko: 비행기가 정해진 경로를 이탈하는 일은 드물어요.
examples.en: It is rare for a plane to leave its set route.
Customers keep leaving, so the company is worried.
I check every day so I don't stray from the plan.

explain: 정해진 길, 줄, 집단, 규칙에서 벗어나 떨어져 나갈 때 써요. 기차는 선로를, 선수는 대열을, 고객은 서비스를 이탈해요. '벗어나다'보다 딱딱하고 뉴스나 업무에서 많이 나와요.
explain_en: Use it when something leaves a set path, line, group or rule. A train leaves its track, a player leaves the formation, a customer leaves a service. It is stiffer than '벗어나다' and common in news and business.

examples.ko: 그 연예인은 논란 뒤에 한동안 잠적했어요.
examples.en: That celebrity went into hiding for a while after the controversy.
Some people disappear because of their debts.

examples.ko: 사장이 갑자기 잠적해서 회사가 문을 닫았대요.
examples.en: I heard the boss suddenly vanished and the company closed down.
Nobody knows where he has gone into hiding.

examples.ko: 잠적하기 전에 한 번만이라도 연락해 주지 그랬어요?
examples.en: Why didn't you at least contact me once before you disappeared?

examples.ko: 한 달째 잠적한 친구에게서 드디어 문자가 왔어요.
examples.en: I finally got a text from my friend who had been out of contact for a month.

explain: 스스로 연락을 끊고 숨는 것이라서 '사라지다'보다 의도가 느껴져요. 보통 사람이나 연예인, 사장처럼 책임을 피하는 상황에서 뉴스에 많이 나와요.
explain_en: It means cutting contact and hiding on one's own, so it carries more sense of intention than '사라지다'. It often appears in the news about people, celebrities or bosses who avoid responsibility.

examples.en: Stamina declines as you get older.
I'm worried because my grades keep dropping.
When you lack sleep, your concentration tends to decline.
The temperature dropped suddenly and my condition got worse.
We exchange products whose quality has declined.

examples.ko: 학습 의욕이 저하되는 시기가 누구에게나 있어요.
examples.en: Everyone has a time when their motivation to study drops.

explain: 저하되다는 능력, 성적, 품질, 의욕, 면역력처럼 좋아야 하는 수준이 내려갈 때 써요. 온도나 가격이 내려가는 일에는 '떨어지다', '내려가다'를 써요. 원인이 있어 낮아지게 하는 쪽은 '저하시키다'예요.
explain_en: 저하되다 is used when a level that ought to be good goes down, such as ability, grades, quality, motivation or immunity. For temperature or price going down use 떨어지다 or 내려가다. The causative form is 저하시키다.

en: distress; being stranded in danger (mountains, sea)

examples.en: A hiker got stranded in the snow.

examples.ko: 조난 신고를 받고 구조대가 바로 출동했어요.
examples.en: The rescue team was dispatched right after receiving the distress report.

examples.ko: 안개가 심한 날에는 조난 위험이 커요.
examples.en: The risk of getting lost and in danger is high on very foggy days.

examples.ko: 조난 신호를 보내려고 휴대폰 손전등을 켰어요.
examples.en: I turned on my phone's flashlight to send a distress signal.

examples.ko: 조난 사고를 막으려면 혼자 산에 가지 마세요.
examples.en: To prevent people from getting stranded in accidents, don't go up the mountain alone.
A helicopter took off to look for the missing climber.

explain: 주로 등산, 바다, 눈보라 같은 자연 속 상황에서 쓰고 '조난(을) 당하다', '조난 신고/신호/사고'처럼 짝말로 나와요. 도시에서 일어난 사고에는 쓰지 않아요. 뉴스나 안전 안내에서 자주 보여요.
explain_en: It is mainly used for situations in nature such as mountains, the sea and snowstorms, and comes in set phrases like '조난(을) 당하다' and '조난 신고/신호/사고'. It is not used for accidents in a city. You often see it in news and safety notices.

examples.ko: 작은 말다툼이 큰 싸움의 촉발이 됐어요.
examples.en: A small argument became the trigger for a big fight.
That incident was what set off the protest.
They are investigating the cause that set it off.
This announcement led to a controversy being set off.
Finding the triggering factor is important.
When was the point at which the economic crisis was set off?

explain: '~의 촉발', '촉발 원인'처럼 다른 말 앞뒤에 붙여 써요. 혼자 쓰기보다 동사 '촉발하다', '촉발되다'가 더 흔해요. 일상에서는 '계기'를 많이 쓰고, '촉발'은 뉴스·보고서 같은 딱딱한 글에서 써요.
explain_en: It is attached to other words, as in '~의 촉발' or '촉발 원인'. The verbs '촉발하다' and '촉발되다' are more common than the noun alone. In daily talk people say '계기'; '촉발' belongs to stiff writing such as news and reports.

examples.en: When fatigue builds up, the body starts to hurt.
Accumulated experience creates skill.
Building up data takes a long time.

examples.ko: 지방 축적을 막으려면 운동을 해야 해요.
examples.en: To prevent fat build-up, you need to exercise.

examples.ko: 부의 축적 방법을 다룬 책을 읽었어요.
examples.en: I read a book about how to accumulate wealth.

examples.ko: 오랜 축적 끝에 이 기술이 나왔어요.
examples.en: This technology came after a long period of accumulation.

explain: 조금씩 쌓여서 많아지는 것을 말하며 '피로 축적', '데이터 축적', '경험 축적'처럼 눈에 안 보이는 것에 자주 써요. 물건을 쌓는 것은 '쌓다'가 자연스러워요. 보통 '축적되다', '축적하다' 형태로 만나요.
explain_en: The gradual piling up of something, mostly intangible things such as fatigue, data, or experience. For physically stacking objects, '쌓다' is more natural. You will most often meet it as 축적되다 or 축적하다.

examples.ko: 이번 실수는 회사에 치명타가 될 수 있어요.
examples.en: This mistake could be a fatal blow to the company.
The injury was a devastating blow to that player.

examples.ko: 환율 상승이 수출 업체에 치명타를 안겼어요.
examples.en: The rise in the exchange rate dealt a heavy blow to exporters.
That rumor was a killer blow to the shop.

examples.ko: 한 번의 거짓말이 신뢰에 치명타를 입혔어요.
examples.en: A single lie dealt a fatal blow to trust.
The heavy rain dealt a serious blow to the farms.

explain: '타격'보다 회복하기 어려울 만큼 크고 심한 피해일 때 써요. '치명타를 입다', '치명타를 주다', '치명타가 되다'처럼 자주 말해요. 복싱 같은 경기에서 결정적으로 맞은 한 방을 말할 때도 써요.
explain_en: Compared with '타격' (a hit), it means damage so serious that recovery is hard. It is often used as '치명타를 입다', '치명타를 주다' or '치명타가 되다'. It can also describe a decisive punch in a sport like boxing.

examples.ko: 여름에는 모기 퇴치 스프레이가 꼭 필요해요.
examples.en: In summer you really need a mosquito repellent spray.

examples.ko: 정부가 질병 퇴치를 위해 예산을 늘렸어요.
examples.en: The government increased its budget to eradicate the disease.
We left the cockroach extermination to a professional company.

examples.ko: 쥐 퇴치에 효과가 좋은 방법이 있어요.
examples.en: There is a method that works well for getting rid of mice.

examples.ko: 마을 사람들은 잡초 퇴치 작업을 함께 했어요.
examples.en: The villagers worked together on clearing out the weeds.
Eradicating the infectious disease is the biggest goal.

explain: '퇴치'는 모기, 쥐, 병처럼 해로운 것을 없앨 때 써요. 약이나 방법을 말할 때 '모기 퇴치제', '해충 퇴치'처럼 앞에 대상을 붙여 써요.
explain_en: 퇴치 is used for getting rid of harmful things like mosquitoes, rats or diseases. For a product or method, put the target first: '모기 퇴치제', '해충 퇴치'.

en: improve; take a turn for the better

examples.en: My health improved after I received treatment.
If the economy improves, jobs will increase.
The patient's condition is improving little by little.

examples.ko: 두 나라의 관계가 호전될 기미가 보여요.
examples.en: There are signs that the relationship between the two countries will improve.
The weather improved, so the plane took off.
The symptoms have not improved yet.

explain: 병세·상황·경기처럼 나쁘던 것이 좋은 쪽으로 바뀔 때 써요. '좋아지다'보다 딱딱해서 뉴스·병원·경제 이야기에 잘 나와요. 반대는 '악화되다'예요.
explain_en: Use it when something bad, like an illness, a situation, or the economy, turns for the better. It is stiffer than 좋아지다 and fits news, hospital, and economy talk. The opposite is 악화되다.

dis.h: illness or economy takes a better turn

p.n: 좋아졌다 is plainer; 호전되다 is formal or medical.

examples.en: Rumors spread quickly on the internet.
A cold spread through our school.

examples.ko: 새로운 유행이 전 세계로 확산하고 있어요.
examples.en: A new trend is spreading around the world.

examples.ko: 나쁜 소문이 확산하지 않게 조심해야 해요.
examples.en: We have to be careful so bad rumors don't spread.
The medical staff were busy trying to stop the spreading infection.

examples.ko: 좋은 습관이 회사 전체로 확산하면 좋겠어요.
examples.en: I hope a good habit spreads across the whole company.

explain: '퍼지다'는 소문, 냄새, 병에 두루 쓰는 일상 말이고, '확산하다'는 뉴스나 보고서에서 범위가 넓어지는 상황에 써요. '확산되다'도 같은 뜻으로 많이 말해요.
explain_en: 퍼지다 is the everyday word for rumors, smells, and illness; 확산하다 is used in news and reports when the range keeps widening. 확산되다 is also common with the same meaning.
